claim: Handing arithmetic and counting to an interpreter beats in-model chain-of-thought, and the gap widens with number size.
agent_test: Same tasks, equal tokens: model-only CoT vs model writes code for counting/sums; add a large-number variant (GSM-HARD style).

claim: The PAL headline gain (+15 over PaLM-540B CoT) mixes models; against the same Codex model with CoT it is +6.4 (72.0 vs 65.6). The robust effect is on large numbers (61.5 vs 20.1).
agent_test: Compare same model with and without code; report the same-model delta, not cross-model.

claim: A small model with a calculator tool beats much larger models without one on zero-shot math (Toolformer 40.4/29.4/44.0 vs GPT-3 175B 14.0/10.0/19.8), but part of the gain comes from the tool-trace finetuning (disabled-tool 9.6/5.0/9.3 vs base 7.5/5.2/9.9).
agent_test: Run the small model with and without the calculator at equal tokens.

claim: Gains from code offloading are smaller when the hard part is translating the problem into a program (AQuA stays 58%; SVAMP +4%).
agent_test: Tag items as calculation-bound vs formulation-bound; expect code gain on the first only.

claim: Models fail multi-step computation held in the model as size grows (3-digit multiplication 55% ChatGPT, 59% GPT-4; accuracy decays toward zero on larger sizes); explicit scratchpads help, but in Faith and Fate the gain shrinks to zero as complexity grows and fine-tuned GPT-3 does not generalise, whereas Nye et al. find scratchpad-trained models improve out-of-distribution on 9-10 digit addition as model size increases.
agent_test: Counting/multiplication at growing size, in-head vs code-held state.
audit_note: Numbers (55%, 59%) match, but 'scratchpads help in distribution only' is too strong: Nye et al. report scratchpad-trained models improve on out-of-distribution 9-10 digit addition with scale; Faith and Fate only find the scratchpad boost diminishes to zero as complexity grows.
claim_before_audit: Models fail multi-step computation held in the model as size grows (3-digit multiplication 55% ChatGPT, 59% GPT-4; near zero on larger sizes); explicit scratchpads help in distribution only.

claim: Code that runs what is runnable and has the model simulate the rest beats code-only and thought-only (Chain of Code 84% on BBH, +12 over CoT; 91% with GPT-4). Code-only fails non-algorithmic tasks.
agent_test: Per sub-step routing: executable steps to code, semantic steps to the model.

claim: In humans, a meta-analysis (abstract only) finds the offloading benefit larger when forced than when chosen, and people over-use reminders from biased confidence. For LLMs the evidence is mixed: forced code usually beats text, model-chosen code (Code Interpreter) beat forced all-code for GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini but not GPT-3.5, and a program-controlled code+text+summary combination was best overall in Chen et al.
agent_test: Arm A: program forces tool at defined steps; arm B: model decides. Equal tokens.
audit_note: Human half holds (Burnett and Richmond abstract: benefit larger when forced; Engeler and Gilbert / Ngai and Gilbert: reminder over-use). But the LLM comparison in Chen et al. is mixed: model-chosen Code Interpreter beat forced all-code for GPT-4o (83.5 vs 80.3) and GPT-4o-mini (80.8 vs 77.4) and lost only for GPT-3.5 (64.5 vs 68.1).
claim_before_audit: Forced or program-controlled offloading beats model-chosen offloading: humans over-use reminders yet choose them from biased confidence; meta-analysis finds the offloading benefit larger when forced than chosen.

claim: Human reminder bias (over-offloading) is only partly explained by underconfidence: calibrating confidence removed the confidence error but not the over-use.
schema_part: G (trigger on measured error, not stated confidence)
agent_test: Do not add self-confidence gating; gate on logged per-task error rates.
audit_note: Minor: Ngai and Gilbert 2026 find a different training (5 trials with feedback) modestly lowers reminder bias, so 'partly explained' fits; Engeler and Gilbert figures match.

claim: Metacognitive training with true performance feedback improves offloading choices slightly (d about .26-.35); predictions alone, fake feedback and single statements do not.
agent_test: Show the agent its measured tool-vs-self error table in context; compare tool routing to no table. Small effect expected.

claim: Offloading is chosen more at higher memory load, longer delay and higher reward, and cheap writes remove the load penalty on accuracy.
schema_part: memory (cheap writes, write always at load)
agent_test: Vary state size; compare write-always vs write-on-demand cost.
audit_note: Higher reward effect appears only as a second-hand citation (Dupont 2021) in Chiu and Gilbert; load, delay and cheap-write findings were checked directly.

claim: Offloading speeds the task but weakens later memory of the offloaded content; an explicit learning goal with forced offloading mostly removes the cost.
schema_part: memory (re-read store, do not rely on recall)
agent_test: After code-held state steps, ask later question needing the content, with and without re-reading the store.

claim: Photo-taking impairment is replicated for paintings (combined d=0.62, 5 photos vs observe) but mixed for lectures (impairment in person, benefit online).
agent_test: Human boundary only; no direct agent test.

claim: The 'Google Stroop' priming effect failed to replicate twice (BF01 about 5 and 9); the where-vs-what recall half is untested.
agent_test: No agent design depends on it.

claim: Smartphone presence has a small negative cognitive effect (g=-0.14), mostly memory, varying by region; heterogeneity is high (I2 61.8%).
agent_test: Not agent-testable.

claim: Saving to an external store frees capacity for new learning, only if the store is trusted (saving-enhanced memory).
agent_test: Write state to store then drop it from context; compare later-step accuracy against keeping it in context.

claim: In a prospective-memory experiment (N=320), people who had experienced a 100% reliable reminder reduced intention-related thinking and retrieved worse when it was unexpectedly withdrawn; in two route-planning experiments, removing an offloading aid hurt performance more than introducing one helped.
schema_part: G (verify store before reliance; build store from step 1)
agent_test: Corrupt or drop the store mid-run; measure recovery with and without store from the start.
audit_note: Let it go (N=320) shows people given a 100% reliable reminder reduced (not stopped) intention-related thoughts and retrieved worse when it was withdrawn; the removal-costs-more result comes from one route-planning task (Florean et al.), not offloading in general.
claim_before_audit: Trusted reliable stores cause people to stop internal maintenance and fail when the store is withdrawn; removing an aid costs more than adding one helps.

claim: Offloading to an LLM in humans lowers recall of own work (83.3% could not quote essay vs 11.1%) and weakens ownership; small N preprint.
agent_test: Human cost; agent analogue is statelessness of the model about what it wrote.

claim: Tool access raises final accuracy but degrades reasoning quality (Tool-Induced Myopia: up to +19.3 points accuracy, non-tool wins up to 41.5% more pairwise reasoning comparisons); errors shift from arithmetic to logic and assumptions. Same-model gains differ: o4-mini +19.3, GPT-4.1 +2.4, GPT-4.1-mini -1.3 final accuracy; a prompt-only fix cost 1.9 of the 2.4 points.
schema_part: G (tool output is evidence, check derivation)
agent_test: Score reasoning-process quality, not only final answer, with and without code.

claim: Unrestricted tool use over-calls; a reward for fewer calls cuts calls up to 68.3% with comparable accuracy.
agent_test: Cap tool calls per task; check accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Paging state between a small context and external stores improves long-memory retrieval (MemGPT: GPT-4 32.1 to 92.5%).
agent_test: Deep-memory retrieval, code store vs context only.

claim: Giving the exact algorithm in the prompt did not rescue reasoning models on puzzles at high complexity (Illusion of Thinking); a reply attributes part of the collapse to token limits and unsolvable cases.
schema_part: G (execute algorithms in code, not in text)
agent_test: Run the algorithm in code vs in text on Hanoi at growing n.

claim: Exact symbolic arithmetic in one forward pass matches code-interpreter accuracy with far fewer tokens (OccamLlama 100.0 vs GPT-4o+code 99.8, 50x fewer generation tokens).
agent_test: Not testable without weight access; use code interpreter.

claim: In a same-model test across 6 LLMs, model-chosen code (Code Interpreter) beat forced code for GPT-4o (83.5 vs 80.3) and GPT-4o-mini (80.8 vs 77.4) but not GPT-3.5 (64.5 vs 68.1); forced code beat text (mean 77.2 vs 73.9). GPT-4o misses code in the medium-difficulty range.
agent_test: Compare told-to-code vs free choice on the same items for our model; log misses in the mid range.

claim: Same-model effect of a code interpreter on hard competition math is not uniform: o4-mini 45.1 to 64.4, GPT-4.1 24.6 to 27.0, GPT-4.1-mini 30.0 to 28.7. Gains come with worse step-level reasoning.
agent_test: Run our model with and without code on the same items; also score reasoning quality, not only the answer.

claim: A one-sentence prompt telling a tool-augmented model to treat code output as hints raised reasoning win rate (45.6 to 52.7) but cut accuracy (27.0 to 25.1) on GPT-4.1: a prompt-only fix removes most of the tool gain.
agent_test: Keep the tool role to state and counts; test whether this limits TIM without the accuracy loss.

claim: Over-calling tools is a measured failure and trained agents cut calls a lot at similar accuracy (OTC-PO up to 68.3% fewer calls; SMART about one-fifth the calls on GSM8K), but all fixes found are trained, not prompt-only. No prompt-only call-budget curve exists for frozen API models.
agent_test: Build the curve ourselves: accuracy and tokens at call caps of 0, 1, 2, 4, unlimited.

claim: Model-written memory records can be poisoned or wrong and agents then follow them (MINJA injection 98.2%, attack success 76.8%; experience-following makes errors propagate). No study measured whether agents detect a corrupted store on their own.
agent_test: Plant a wrong value in the code store and measure whether the agent notices; require program-checked writes.
audit_note: MINJA (Dong, He, Tang, Xiang et al.) and the experience-following paper (Xiong, He, Tang, Xiang et al.) share authors Pengfei He, Jiliang Tang and Zhen Xiang, so they are one research group; numbers 98.2% and 76.8% do match MINJA.

claim: Clearing stale tool results from context while keeping a memory tool improved a vendor agentic-search benchmark (+29% context editing, +39% with memory tool, 84% fewer tokens, Claude Sonnet 4.5), but no peer-reviewed test of clearing with vs without a re-read step exists; the human cost of unexpected store loss (Burnett 2026) argues for keeping a re-read path.
agent_test: Run: clear after write, with and without a forced re-read at the next step.

claim: Forced offloading beats choice offloading in a human meta-analysis (Burnett & Richmond 2026) and equalises people across working-memory capacity, but the effect sizes, k and forced-minus-chosen gap are unread (abstract only).
agent_test: Treat direction as supported and size as unknown; do not quote a magnitude.

claim: A code-generated solution to Tower of Hanoi (15 disks, Lua function) is reported to succeed across four frontier models in under 5,000 tokens, which answers the token-limit critique for the generator but is unquantified and untested as a state-tracking loop.
schema_part: G (execute algorithms in code, not in text)
agent_test: Measure it: Hanoi at growing n, algorithm in text vs executed by code, counts of successes.
